reason: The first two proposals preserve all four ZA accumulators and target vector reuse through MOPA scheduling, with low correctness risk and no extra ZA state. Their benefit is uncertain because the compiler may already schedule the same way. Next are loop/codegen changes that preserve the reduction structure; the measured pointer experiments were inconclusive, so they do not justify a stronger ranking. Transpose and layout experiments may help memory access but add broader changes, scratch traffic, or tail risk. Packing adds cost, and merging streaming regions ranks last given the prior severe regression, whose cause remains unknown.
